review_notes: Read the whole file and the sibling lemmas it uses (glin_pow_of_eqOn, grng_inv, eq_zero_of_mem_grng, exists_mem_restrict). All the repetition is inside one long proof, between the y₁ and y₂ pieces. Most of it is short (hperp₁/hperp₂, hU₁₂/hU₂₁, hz*koff, which are one-liners). The only block with real content is the per-piece restriction data: hcyc, z≠1, and the exists_mem_restrict call. The repetition is modest and does not appear in a second declaration, so the case for a shared lemma is weak. I did not see the type name of the GenPieceSet hypothesis, so I only sketched the lemma's signature. I checked nothing by compiling.

findings.problem: The same argument is written out once for y₁ and once for y₂. In each copy it takes the cyclic-generation hypothesis hS.cyc and rewrites it through the restriction z of a piece generator, using glin_pow_of_eqOn. It then shows z ≠ 1 from a nonzero vector in grng y, using eq_zero_of_mem_grng. The two copies differ only by the index 1/2. The related exists_mem_restrict calls at lines 82–85 and the grng_inv facts at lines 80–81 repeat in the same way. The proof is already very long, and these copies make it harder to see that the two pieces are treated symmetrically.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one lemma next to glin_pow_fix. For hA : GenMax (polB Q) (matrixDerived Q) p A, a piece set S with hS (the same type as in the proof) and y ∈ S, it would give ∃ z ∈ A, (∀ x ∈ grng y, glin z x = glin y x) ∧ (∀ v ∈ (grng y).orthogonalBilin (polB Q), glin z v = v) ∧ z ≠ 1 ∧ (∀ c ∈ A, ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ x ∈ grng y, glin c x = glin (z ^ k) x).

Proof sketch:
1. Apply hA.exists_mem_restrict with nondegOn_grng hA hy and grng_inv hA hy.
2. For cyc, take k from hS.cyc and rewrite with glin_pow_of_eqOn (grng_inv hA hy hy) hzon.
3. For z ≠ 1, pick x ≠ 0 in grng y using grng_ne_bot (hS.ne_one y hyS). If z = 1, then hzon gives glin y x = x, so eq_zero_of_mem_grng gives x = 0, a contradiction.

In the main proof, replace lines 80–107 with two obtains, `obtain ⟨z₁, hz₁A, hz₁on, hz₁off, hz₁1, hcyc₁⟩ := piece_restrict_data hA hS hy₁S` and the same for y₂. The x₁/x₂ vectors are still needed at lines 266–267 (hx₁, hx₁0), so keep the `hne` choice or return one nonzero vector from the lemma.
findings.benefit: The only nontrivial per-piece argument (cyc through restriction, plus z ≠ 1) is proved and checked once. The 70-odd-line main proof gets shorter and its y₁/y₂ symmetry is visible. A fix to the piece argument would be made in one place. The lemma could also be reused by sibling files that handle other pieces of the same terminal piece set.
